changes.what: Rebuilt the address.country transform: added an `upper` step, upper-cased the map keys, moved `case_insensitive` inside `args`, and added more ISO mappings (Singapore, New Zealand, and others).
changes.why: All 439 non-empty Country values failed with 'not in map', including plain 'Australia' and 'AUSTRALIA'. The lower-case keys never matched, and the top-level `case_insensitive` flag was evidently ignored. Upper-casing first and using upper-case keys no longer depends on that flag. Singapore also failed because it was not in the map, so I added common countries. Values still not in the map (junk such as a phone number) are dropped rather than defaulted.

changes.what: Kept the postcode mapping as is.
changes.why: The single error ('139658', 0.2%) is a genuinely invalid postcode that should be dropped, and it is well under the 5% threshold.

changes.what: Added reviewer notes about the country map and about an anonymised-looking legal name in the preview.
changes.why: A reviewer should know that countries outside the map are dropped, and that a legal name like '847219-X8N0N9- PAF' is passed through as source-stated with no ABN.

changes.what: address.country: moved the map_values arguments (map, case_insensitive) to the top level of the transform object, so it is {"op": "map_values", "map": {...}, "case_insensitive": true}. Previously they were nested under an "args" key.
changes.why: The vocabulary shape is {"op": name, ...args}, so arguments sit beside "op". The engine most likely never saw my nested map and treated it as empty. That fits the error "value 'AUSTRALIA' not in map" on 100% of values, even for 'Australia' and after the upper transform. The round-1 failure had the same symptom, so case sensitivity was probably not the real cause. I kept the upper-cased keys and case_insensitive as a belt-and-braces measure.

changes.what: Lowered entity.website confidence from 0.75 to 0.65 and made the rationale more explicit.
changes.why: The preview shows BHL DALYELLUP TWO APARTMENTS LTD with the website of its parent, bethanie.com.au. A website column that is sometimes a parent's or related organisation's site is not reliably the entity's own website, so the confidence was too high.

changes.what: Updated the country note in notes to reflect the likely root cause.
changes.why: The earlier note blamed case sensitivity; the more probable cause was the misplaced argument nesting.
